NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a monitoring/indication scheme via periodic VSWR measurement and threshold-based alerts.  
Departure: Electrochemical corrosion potential mapping using in-situ pH and conductivity to predict VSWR drift before it exceeds threshold.  
Failure-physics connection: Contact corrosion in coastal environments is electrochemical; pH and conductivity directly govern corrosion kinetics, enabling early detection of corrosive conditions that cause VSWR drift.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Corrosion current density i_corr (A/m²) = exp[(αF/RT)(E_corr - E_0)], where E_corr depends on electrolyte conductivity and pH (per Butler-Volmer and Nernst equations).  
Magnitude verification: For seawater (conductivity ~5 S/m, pH ~8), E_corr shifts ~100 mV per pH unit; a 50 mV shift correlates with ~0.1 Ω contact resistance increase, detectable via in-situ sensors before VSWR exceeds threshold.

Pass/fail threshold: Corrosion potential shift >50 mV must precede VSWR increase >0.1 Ω by >48 hours.  
Duration: 30 days (covers multiple tidal cycles).  
Kill criterion: If VSWR increases before predicted by sensor data, mechanism fails.

Primary stated indicator: VSWR (defines failure threshold). Secondary indicator: pH/conductivity (supplements by predicting drift).
